The substitutions \(t=e^{h/k}\) and \(x=e^{l/(k-1)}\) are bijective and reduce the system to two positive-root polynomials. Descartes' rule gives an upper bound of three roots at each stage, while explicit sign brackets for \(k\ge4\), \(\theta>24\) give three distinct roots at each stage. The nine pairs therefore exhaust this branch. The finite checker is supplemental.

value.rationale: The source itself flags the \(b=0\) multiplicity as potentially larger than three but leaves it unresolved. The theorem converts that qualitative observation into an exact nine-solution count on a natural coupled matrix family, uniformly for every tree order \(k\ge4\) in an explicit low-temperature region. This is a structural phase-count result, not a routine recomputation or a single numerical example.
